newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow city to raise $4 bln in paper by end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Moscow city to raise $4 bln in paper by end 1997.

text.p: Russia's capital city plans to raise 20-25 trillion roubles ($3.7-$4.6 billion) by the end of 1997, beginning with 11 trillion roubles of domestic bonds and a $400-$500 million Eurobond, a city official said on Wednesday.

City municipal loan department spokesman Mikhail Chernyshov told Reuters that Moscow would issue eight trillion roubles in domestic bonds and an additional three trillion roubles in savings bonds as well as the Eurobond by the end of December.
"The Eurobond volume is not that much by international standards," Chernyshov said, describing Moscow's first international issue as a "trial balloon".
"We want to show foreign investors that we are ready to borrow on world-accepted terms."
Moscow would make further Eurobond issues dependent on the success of the first, he added.
Chernyshov said Moscow had decided to follow Russia's lead in applying for a credit rating before it issued the Eurobond.

"After Russia received a sovereign rating, we decided it would be good to have a rating, too," he said. "Only three weeks ago we did not plan this, as Nomura and CS First Boston guaranteed sales of the issue."
He said the city had not yet chosen agencies for the rating.
Nomura International Plc and CS First Boston will lead-manage the issue on international markets and Alfa-Bank and Stolichny Bank Sberezheny will act as joint leads in Russia.
Moody's, Standard & Poor's and IBCA have recently assigned Russia better-than-expected credit ratings, giving its first Eurobond a speculative grade status.

Chernyshov said the funds raised from the issues would be used to finance investment projects in the city chosen by a special committee from 3,500 projects, by their quickness, profitability and usefullness for the capital.
